items.title: Fed minutes: Another rate hike likely coming this year to combat persistent inflation
items.summary: Most Federal Reserve officials expect another interest rate increase will likely be needed this year to combat inflation, according to the central bank's meeting minutes.

items.title: Week Ahead: US inflation data, major bank earnings to drive Wall Street
items.summary: September Consumer Price Index report in focus as investors assess prospects of Federal Reserve rate hike in December

items.title: Wall Street Week Ahead: Bank earnings, CPI headline busy markets week as S&P 500 hovers near records
items.summary: U.S. stock investors are on high alert as they anticipate quarterly earnings reports from major banks, including JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs. These reports are pivotal, shedding light on corporate profitability and the future direction of interest rates. The upcoming Consumer Price Index report will also provide vital clues about inflation trends, potentially swaying Federal Reserve policy.

items.title: Gold hits one-week high, heads for weekly gain on bargain-hunting
items.summary: Gold prices surged as investors seized the opportunity to buy low after a recent dip to a two-month low. Currently, spot gold has ascended to around $4,190.49 and is on track for a weekly increase. Traders are closely monitoring potential interest rate adjustments by the US Federal Reserve. Analysts suggest a possible test of the $4,000 support level if inflation continues to be a factor.

items.title: Treasuries Slip on Inflation Worry as Energy Costs Stay High
items.summary: Treasuries slipped at the end of the week as still-elevated energy costs stoked concern about inflation and backed expectations for further Federal Reserve interest-rate increases.

items.title: US Fed's Waller expects more rate hikes as inflation stays elevated
items.summary: US Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller has indicated that further interest rate hikes are likely in the coming months as inflation remains stubbornly above the central bank's 2 per cent target, although the timing and pace of increases will depend on incoming economic data.
